chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: Lonnie Johnson pays $50 each, which settles Tate on music
summary: Johnson pays each player fifty dollars, which convinces Tate to become a musician; he later saw Johnson in Toronto.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: playing, he calls me over into the corner -- I don't know why he chose me -- he says -- he gave me $50.00. In those days, the dollar bills were much larger than now and fifty, it looked like you had a thousand.

And it was a lot of money then. People were working for like $50.00 a month. I remember that. So anyway, I called the five guys over -- we had five pieces -- he says, "What are you doing?" I says, "Well, I got to pay them." I says, "It's $10.00 apiece." So he says, "No, that's yours." He says, "I'm going to give them fifty." He gave us $300.00, you know, I mean, like -- $250.00. Man, when he said that, my heart stopped. I says, "Man, this man --" I says, "Are you sure?" He says, "Yeah." He says, "It's fifty for each one of them." Then that made up my mind. I says, "There's no way for me to top this in anything," so I says, "This is it." So, you know, that's the truth. This is actually the truth.

In later years, before he died, he remembered it and I used to see him in Toronto all the time and he did very good in Toronto. He was in good health and everything until somebody drove up on the sidewalk and hit him and broke both of his hips in a car and he was kind of old and he didn't get well after that. But up until then, he was doing fine. Worked all the time in Toronto and everything, loved him in Toronto. But he hasn't been dead for about seven, eight years.
And that's one thing that really made up my mind.
Yeah. I says, 'I can't beat this.' (Laughter.)
